transcript.text: To solve this equivalent fractions problem, one must apply the fundamental principle of fractions, which states that multiplying the numerator and denominator by the same non-zero integer preserves proportionality. First, ascertain the factor by which the denominator scales by dividing six by three, yielding two. Subsequently, multiply the numerator, two, by this exact scalar factor of two. Consequently, the unknown numerator is four, establishing the equivalence of two-thirds and four-sixths.

Regarding the summation of two-ninths and four-ninths, since both fractions share a common denominator, one simply aggregates the numerators while retaining the denominator unchanged. Therefore, you compute two plus four, which equals six, resulting in six-ninths. This resultant fraction should subsequently be reduced to its simplest form by dividing both terms by their greatest common divisor, which is three, yielding two-thirds as the final simplified answer.

To calculate one-fourth plus one-eighth, one must first establish a common denominator, as the current denominators are heterogeneous. The least common multiple of four and eight is eight. Convert one-fourth by multiplying its numerator and denominator by two, yielding two-eighths. Subsequently, compute the sum of two-eighths and one-eighth by adding their numerators, resulting in three-eighths, which is already in its irreducible simplest form.
